classification.difficultyReason: Model a variable triangle perimeter and use auxiliary-angle amplitude to establish its maximum.

content.prompt: $AB$ is a diameter of a semi-circle with radius $R$. A point $P$ is moving on the circumference. Let $\angle PAB=\theta$.

spec.sourceRegion: Right column, question 10, between the stem and parts.
spec.description: Unshaded upper semicircle with horizontal diameter AB, an upper-right point P, chords AP and PB, a right-angle mark at P and theta inside angle PAB.
spec.mathematics: P lies on the semicircle with diameter AB, so AP is perpendicular to PB. The illustrative coordinate angle locates P without introducing a numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied geometry, point labels and theta are visible; no derived side lengths or maximum are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the perimeter of $\triangle ABP$ in terms of $R$ and $\theta$.

answer.worked:
The angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so $\angle APB=90^\circ$ and $AB=2R$.

$$\begin{align*}AP&=2R\cos\theta\\BP&=2R\sin\theta\\\text{Perimeter}&=2R+2R\cos\theta+2R\sin\theta\\\text{Perimeter}&=2R(1+\sin\theta+\cos\theta).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: As $\theta$ varies, find the maximum perimeter of $\triangle ABP$.

answer.short:
$2R(1+\sqrt2)$, attained at $\theta=\frac\pi4$.

Write $\sin\theta+\cos\theta=\sqrt2\cos(\theta-\frac\pi4)$ and use the maximum cosine value of $1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\sin\theta+\cos\theta&=\sqrt2\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right)\\\text{Perimeter}&=2R\left[1+\sqrt2\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi4\right)\right].\end{align*}$$

Since $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$, the cosine reaches $1$ at $\theta=\frac\pi4$.

$$\text{Maximum perimeter}=2R(1+\sqrt2).$$
